name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 21, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on March
21, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March, 18, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the

City Council Minutes  1  March 21, 2011
   Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

The announcement was provided under City Attorney’s Report.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Musical Presentation

  Lisa Tredwell, member of the Cultural Arts Committee, played the flute.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers, for their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Leckness presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Alicia Brillhart for volunteer
  hours at the Mission Viejo Library. (2) Vistasp Shroff for volunteer hours at the Mission
  Viejo Library; (3) Marlene Kazen for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray
  Community and Senior Center; (4) Edith Murray for volunteer hours at the Norman P.
  Murray Community and Senior Centers; and (5) Betty Saunders for volunteer hours at the
  Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center. Library volunteer Bunny Smith was
  unable to attend the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Mayor Gary Capata and Mayor Pro Tem Paul Glaab, Laguna Niguel: thanked the City Council
and staff for continued cooperation and collaboration with the City of Laguna Niguel on the
widening of Crown Valley Parkway.

David Russell Ohrn ("Dro,") Laguna Niguel: announced that he joined Laguna Niguel Mayor
Capata and Mayor Pro Tem Glaab to see how things are going in Mission Viejo. He has
attended 1,322 City Council Meetings since 1968 and he stated that it was a pleasure to be in
Mission Viejo this evening.

Lisa Ball, Senior Public Information Specialist for South Coast Air Quality Management
District, Rancho Santa Margarita: presented the City Council with a copy of the AQMD’s "State
of the Air 2011" DVD.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked the City Council for a no vote on the request for annexation by
Standard Pacific Homes and stated that it would promote urban sprawl.

City Council Minutes  2  March 21, 2011
 Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: commended the City Council for partnering with other cities, on a
regular basis, to give opportunities for both cities and to be good neighbors.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 11, 13 and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Number not used

4.  Check Register dated February 25, 2011, in the amount of $2,434,652.72

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated March 4, 2011, in the amount of $374,517.26

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Claims Against the City - Gregory Schaefers and Jodi Schaefers

  (1) Rejected the claim filed by Gregory Schaefers; and (2) rejected the claim filed by Jodi
  Schaefers.

7.  Claim Against the City - Stephanie Bolton on Behalf of Anastasia Bolton, Deceased

  Rejected the claim.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2011

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  March 21, 2011
 9.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2011

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2011

  Received and filed.

12.  Oso Creek Restoration Project (CIP 207) - Marguerite Parkway Median Island
  Renovations-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and
  to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days respectively
  after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or
  liens being filed with or by the City; and (3) authorized the payment of the final retention
  of $10,505.15, 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

15.  Crown Valley Parkway Widening-Cabot Road to I-5 (CIP 795)

  (1) Approved the Construction Contract between the City of Laguna Niguel, the City of
  Mission Viejo, the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo
  (CDA), and Ortiz Enterprises, Inc., including Mission Viejo’s cost share of $1,493,035;
  (2) approved the Agreement for Professional Services with the City of Laguna Niguel
  and Caltrop Corporation for construction management services, including Mission
  Viejo’s cost share of $239,255; (3) approved the Agreement for Professional Services
  with the City of Laguna Niguel and RBF Consulting for construction support services,
  including Mission Viejo’s cost share of $41,996; (4) approved the Third, Fourth and Fifth
  Amendments to the agreement with the City of Laguna Niguel and RBF Consulting for
  professional design services, including Mission Viejo’s cost shares in the respective
  amounts of $20,973, $32,215, and $39,950; (5) authorized reimbursement to the City of
  Laguna Niguel in the amount of $18,375 for right-of-way acquisition; (6) authorized
  reimbursement to the City of Laguna Niguel for other construction-related costs not to
  exceed a total of $252,000; and (7) adopted CDA Resolution 11-07 Amending the Fiscal
  Year 2010-2011 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 795.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  4  March 21, 2011
 16.  Reduction in Outstanding Community Development Agency Tax Allocation Notes
  Held By City

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the Governor is questioning the legality and validity of
  asset transfers taking place after January 1, 2011, and he urged the City Council to use
  caution with CDA funds.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to adopt
  CDA Resolution 11-08 Amending the Community Development Agency (CDA) Fiscal
  Year 2010-11 Budget for Costs Related to a Possible Reduction in the Outstanding
  $1.525 million Tax Allocation Notes (TANs).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she had used an incorrect title for Celeste Brady but
  the Minutes correctly refer to Ms. Brady as Special Counsel under items 14 and 15 on
  pages 5 and 6. Council Member Schlicht asked that "Mr. Lieberman" be changed to Dr.
  Lieberman on page 9 and she stated that an important part of the discussion was
  eliminated from the Minutes and one gets the feel that Fun With Chalk is supporting the
  City’s street painting fair.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to direct the City Clerk to amend the minutes
  on page 9, under City Manager's Report, and add Mr. Wilberg's admission that Dr.
  Lieberman is not helping to obtain artists for the City's chalk festival. The motion died
  for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
  the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 7, 2011, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht

City Council Minutes  5  March 21, 2011
   ABSENT: None

11.  General Plan Progress Report for 2010

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  receive and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

13.  CDBG 2010 Residential Asphalt Overlays (CIP 839) Notice of Completion

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to provide a description of the different street repair
  processes in order to educate the public.

  City Engineer Schlesinger described the difference between slurry seal and asphalt
  overlay.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1)
  certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorize payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

14.  Change Order #1 to the Contract with California Yellow Cab to Provide Senior
  Citizen Transportation Services

  Kelly Doyle, Director of Recreation and Community Services, presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  6  March 21, 2011
   Council Member Reardon noted that there will be no funding taken from the City's
  General Fund but rather from the Senior Citizen Operating Fund.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve Change Order #1 and an increase in Purchase Order #110103 from $25,000 to
  $40,000 for Senior Citizen Transportation Services for FY 2010-11.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that he had nothing to report.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that Anthony Horowitz, author of the Alex Rider Adventures,
will visit Mission Viejo tomorrow evening at 7:00 p.m. in the City Council Chamber. On
Wednesday, April 23, Kristi Yamaguchi will visit the Murray Community Center at 6:30 p.m. to
discuss and sign her book “Dream Big Little Pig.” Mr. Wilberg reminded the Council and
residents that the Tee it Up for Marines golf tournament will be held at Camp Pendleton, Friday,
April 25. He also announced that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee is hosting a new event
this year called Up in the Air on Saturday, April 2. Lastly, Mr. Wilberg drew the Councils
attention to the spring/summer Outlook which will be delivered to residents this week and he
thanked Karen Hamman for her efforts with the publication.

Council Member Schlicht asked the City Manager for a report on underground gas lines in
Mission Viejo. She also read an email from a resident who is concerned with missing scrolls and
mission bells on some of the street lights.

City Council Minutes  7  March 21, 2011
 City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she and Mayor Leckness attended a Mission Viejo
Activities Committee recognition event yesterday and she commended the Activities Committee
volunteers for the putting on such wonderful and significant events in the City of Mission Viejo.
She encouraged residents to volunteer with the Activities Committee and to contact her for more
information. She announced that the committee is holding a first-time event called Up In the Air
on Saturday, April 2, on the Village Green at the Murray Community Center. There will be arts
and crafts, balloons, bubble stations, kites, food, music, raffles and prizes. She also announced
that Bunny Days will be held on April 23 from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., Arts Alive Festival is
planned for April 28 through May 1, and a Red Cross Blood Drive will be held on April 19 from
10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center. Council
Member Kelley highlighted the Mission Viejo Outlook which will be delivered to homes and
businesses this week. She thanked City Clerk Karen Hamman for creating the publication and
commended her for her special talents and creativity. Council Member Kelley announced that
everyone was shocked at the earthquake and tsunami in Japan and she and Mayor Leckness are
trying to find a way for Mission Viejo residents to help and reach out. She will return with an
announcement when there is more information to share. She also reminded residents that
monetary donations are always needed at the Red Cross.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon thanked staff for their patience and help and she gave special
recognition to Executive Assistant Jennifer Myers for her time and support. She announced that
she attended the recent Planning and Transportation Commission meeting to express her support
for Commissioner Richard Schweinberg who was leaving after six years of service. She was also
pleased to see the swearing-in of her new appointee, Cliff Swan. Council Member Reardon
attended the Quiznos re-opening on Jeronimo and she, along with Council Member Schlicht, met
with UDR and their architect to discuss their plans for development of the former K-Mart site.
She was able to express her concerns about the number of units they plan to build and the
increase in density, as well as moving from owner-occupied units to rentals. Council Member
Reardon said that she encouraged the developer to meet with the residents of nearby Palmia and
she stated that overall, it was a very good meeting. Council Member Reardon announced that

City Council Minutes  8  March 21, 2011
 flag football season has begun and her grandson has joined a team that is being coached by John
Burns, a former Mission Viejo High School football star. She also relayed to Mayor Leckness
that a resident contacted her with concern about the public donation box that is proposed on
Olympiad Road near the Olympic finish line. She is worried about potential vandalism and she
reminded City Attorney Curley that she had asked about a possible conflict of interest with the
donation box being slated for the Rotary Club. Lastly, Council Member Reardon announced that
the young cancer-stricken boy she continues to talk about is improving and he should be walking
out of the hospital soon. She also asked for continued prayers, support and good thoughts for
young Kaylee who is two years old and undergoing chemotherapy.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked for a report on underground gas lines in the City and she asked
about replacement of the mission bell street lights that are damaged or fall down after an
accident. She stated that the City needs to protect and preserve the traditional values that created
this award-winning community and she asked about the protocol for replacing the bells and
scrolls.

City Manager Wilberg announced that in past years there was a limited amount of money in the
replacement budget but that money was cut from the budget so currently, the City is not
replacing the bells and scrolls. He noted that staff can provide information on the number of
bells and scrolls that need to be replaced during upcoming budget discussions.

Council Member Schlicht thanked the City Manager for his February/March newsletter. She
commented on the list of contracts and stated that she would like the City to go out for bid on the
projects.

Mr. Wilberg confirmed that the city is out to bid on the contracts and the notice in the newsletter
was intended to be an update and to let the Council know when they can expect to see the
agreements on an agenda for approval.

Council Member Schlicht discussed the timeline for the UDR apartments and announced that the
CEQA process begins in May so the public can make comments at that time. The developer
intends to hold a Planning Commission public hearing in either June or July and to come before
the City Council in August. Council Member Schlicht expressed her thanks to Richard
Schweinberg for his service on the Planning and Transportation Commission and stated that our
thoughts and prayers are with the people of Japan as they struggle to put their lives back
together. She encouraged Mission Viejo residents to get survival gear and cash so they are ready
in the event of a disaster. Council Member Schlicht thanked resident Steve Serra for his years of
work on E-Verify and she announced that the first report indicates that 100% of the City’s
contractors are in compliance. She also discussed her attendance at the recent meeting of the
SRA (Saddleback Republican Committee) and she announced that they are hosting the annual
TEA Party on April 15, 2011, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. on the corners of La Paz and Marguerite.
The SRA is also hosting Congressman Gary Miller next month on April 21 and the location is to
be determined. Council Member Schlicht stated that the Council is responsible for making sure

City Council Minutes  9  March 21, 2011
 that the public record is accurate. She believes that public disclosure and public consent makes
for a stronger city and she encouraged more people to become involved. She concluded her
comments with a quote from Thomas Jefferson: “He who permits himself to tell a lie once, finds
it much easier to do it a second and third time, till at length it becomes habitual; he tells lies
without attending to it, and truths without the world´s believing him.”

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury noted that there has been a request for a report on underground gas pipes
and he reminded the Council Members that they received an extensive report late last year and
that would be a good place to start, rather than having staff gather additional information. He
also announced that he is looking forward to the Marine golf tournament this weekend.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness followed-up on Council Member Schlicht’s question and asked the City
Manager about the light standards that are damaged in an accident. He asked if he understood
correctly that the scroll and bells are not being replaced.

City Manager Wilberg announced that the City is responsible for replacing those but money is
not currently budgeted for that purpose. He noted that if there is an accident, the City attempts to
get reimbursement from the driver’s insurance company but those that age and fall off are not
replaced.

Mayor Leckness commended Council Member Reardon for asking questions of staff, prior to the
Council Meeting, and then reviewing the information for public disclosure during the meeting.
He stated that that is exactly the way it should be done. Mayor Leckness encouraged residents to
attend Kristi Yamaguchi’s book presentation and signing on April 23 and the Up in the Air event
on April 2. He also recapped his Walk with the Mayor last weekend. It’s a Grind donated
coffee, Einstein Bagels supplied food, and Casta del Sol golf course provided a golf cart that led
the way as the group walked around Lake Mission Viejo. He stated that it was a fantastic day
and he thanked those who participated. Mayor Leckness concluded his comments by thanking
the residents that attend City Council Meetings and he thanked flutist Lisa Tredwell who opened
the meeting this evening.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour or 8:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 4, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 4, 2011

City Council Minutes  10  March 21, 2011
